title: Kernel formula for product components
statement:
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, outcome space $\Omega=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\Omega_i$, and coordinate weights $w_i$. For any coordinate set $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$, its $S$-component satisfies
\[
f_S(x)=\sum_{y\in\Omega}\left(\prod_{i\in S}\bigl(\mathbf 1_{\{x_i=y_i\}}-w_i(y_i)\bigr)\prod_{i\notin S}w_i(y_i)\right)f(y).
\]
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces
Each coordinate atom mass is strictly positive and coordinate masses sum to one
$S$ is a subset of the coordinate indices
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with coordinate weights $w_i$, $S\subseteq[n]$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Its orthogonal component satisfies $f_S(x)=\sum_y[\prod_{i\in S}(\mathbf1_{x_i=y_i}-w_i(y_i))\prod_{i\notin S}w_i(y_i)]f(y)$.
